states.speech: P = (-3, 2): Quadrant II. Exchanging their order gives (2, -3). Read x first, then y. Both coordinates use the same unit. Axis points belong to no quadrant. The horizontal-then-vertical path explains the ordered pair; its length is not generally the straight-line distance.

P = (5, 0): x-axis. Exchanging their order gives (0, 5). Read x first, then y. Both coordinates use the same unit. Axis points belong to no quadrant. The horizontal-then-vertical path explains the ordered pair; its length is not generally the straight-line distance.

P = (2, 1): Quadrant I. Opposite corner Q = (6, 4). Width = 4, height = 3 units; area = 12 square units. Perimeter = 14 units. Remaining corners: (6, 1) and (2, 4). Read x first, then y. Both coordinates use the same unit. Axis points belong to no quadrant. The rectangle sides are parallel to the axes. Opposite corners may be supplied in either order. Area counts square units; perimeter measures boundary length.

P = (1, 4): Quadrant I. Q = (7, 4). Signed changes: Δx = 6, Δy = 0. Straight-line distance = 6 units; horizontal-plus-vertical path = 6 units. Read x first, then y. Coincident points have distance zero.
